props.yes: An income tax increase on high-income earners in place since 2012 would become permanent instead of expiring in 2031.
props.no: An income tax increase on high-income earners in place since 2012 would expire in 2031.
props.yes_side: The state's largest teachers union (CalMatters, not named in article)
props.no_side: Opponents not named in sources found

props.title: Repeals Prohibition Against Public Funding of Election Campaigns. Legislative Statute.
props.yes: State and local governments could create public campaign financing programs for candidates for public office.
props.no: State and most local governments would remain unable to create public campaign finance programs.
props.yes_side: California Democratic Party (CalMatters); placed on ballot by Legislature (SB 42, Umberg)
props.no_side: Opponents not named in sources found

props.title: Changes Recall Election Process for Statewide Officers. Legislative Constitutional Amendment.
props.yes: Recall elections would no longer include a question about who should fill the vacancy.
props.no: Voters would continue to be asked who should fill the vacancy as part of recall elections.
props.yes_side: Democratic Party (CalMatters); placed on ballot by Legislature (SCA 1, Newman)

props.title: Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes. Initiative Statute.
props.yes: The state would create a new homebuying assistance program.
props.no: The state would not be required to create a new homebuying assistance program.
props.yes_side: Unions, real estate developers, Democratic Party (CalMatters)
props.no_side: Opponents not named in sources found

props.title: Authorizes Bonds for Immunology Medical Research. Initiative Statute.
props.yes: The state could borrow $8.4 billion to support medical research in immunology and immunotherapy.
props.no: The state could not borrow $8.4 billion to support medical research in immunology and immunotherapy.
props.yes_side: Placed on ballot by Gary K. Michelson (CalMatters)
props.no_side: Opponents not named in sources found

props.title: Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
props.yes: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
props.no: A voter's identity would continue to be established with the voter's signature.
props.yes_side: Reform California with Carl DeMaio, California Republican Party; top funders Richard Uihlein ($17.0M), Joseph Gebbia ($8.0M); $36.7M total (KQED, Nov 1)
props.no_side: No on 39, California Democratic Party, California Nurses Association, League of Women Voters of CA, Common Cause; $35.2M total (KQED, Nov 1)

props.title: Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers. Initiative Constitutional Amendment and Statute.
props.yes: The state would collect a one-time tax from billionaires equal to 5 percent of their wealth.
props.no: The state would not collect a one-time tax from billionaires equal to 5 percent of their wealth.
props.yes_side: YES on 40 - Billionaire Tax Now (SEIU United Healthcare Workers West), about $32.0M
props.no_side: No on Prop 40 committee, about $118.8M, nearly all from Building a Better California (largest donor Sergey Brin); Golden State Promise ($10.45M); business leaders and Planned Parenthood also oppose (CalMatters)

props.title: Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
props.yes: New state taxes could not be excluded from the state spending limit, and the State Auditor would review programs funded by proposed new special taxes (LAO, paraphrased; a yes vote also invalidates Prop 40 per CalMatters).
props.no: The State Auditor's responsibility to review government programs and the state spending limit requirements would not change.
props.yes_side: Yes on 41 - Californians for Transparency and Accountability, about $58.4M, nearly all from Building a Better California
props.no_side: Working Families Say NO to Propositions 41 and 42 (labor unions), about $951K

props.title: Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
props.yes: The state could not establish new taxes on the ownership of financial assets or other personal property.
props.no: The state would continue to have the option to establish new taxes on the ownership of financial assets.
props.yes_side: Yes on 42 - Protect Retirement & Life Savings, about $128.0M, nearly all from Building a Better California
props.no_side: Working Families Say NO to Propositions 41 and 42 (labor unions), about $951K

props.title: Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services. Legislative Constitutional Amendment.
props.yes: Certain local government taxes would require two-thirds approval by voters.
props.no: Certain local government taxes could continue to be approved by voters with a majority vote.
props.yes_side: Placed on ballot by Legislature (ACA 22, Wicks); proponents not named in sources found
props.no_side: Opponents not named in sources found

props.title: Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% of Revenue on Program Services. Initiative Statute.
props.yes: Certain private nonprofit health care clinics would have to spend at least 90 percent of their revenue on program services.
props.no: The new requirement on health care clinic spending would not go into effect.
props.no_side: Democratic Party and health care associations (CalMatters)

props.title: Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects. Initiative Statute.
props.yes: Certain public and private projects would be eligible for new project review and court challenge procedures.
props.no: Public and private projects would continue to use existing project review and court challenge procedures.

boe.note: Open seat. District 1 runs through the Central Valley and inland California. Esparza is Fresno City Council president (termed out of his council seat); Grove is the former Senate Republican leader from Bakersfield. Statewide and Valley county numbers from the Secretary of State.

a_case.text: Endorsed by Rep. Jim Costa and backed by the Democratic Party in a district Democrats have held

b_case.text: Former Senate Republican leader with a Bakersfield base in the district's most Republican counties
